methods.name: Mendenhall's Characteristic Curves of Composition
methods.formula_summary: P(L = k) = count(|w| = k) / N for k in 1..max_len
methods.description: Pioneering stylometric fingerprint measuring the relative frequency distribution of word lengths (1-letter, 2-letter, ..., k-letter words). Applied by Mendenhall (1887, 1901) to Shakespeare, Marlowe, and Bacon.

methods.name: Lexical Richness & Vocabulary Diversity Indices
methods.authors: G. U. Yule (1944), E. H. Simpson (1949), P. Guiraud (1954), A. Honoré (1979), M. A. Covington & J. D. McFall (2010)
methods.formula_summary: TTR = V/N; Guiraud R = V/sqrt(N); Yule's K = 10^4 * (sum(i^2 * V_i) - N) / N^2; MATTR(W)
methods.description: Quantifies an author's vocabulary richness and repetition rate independent of text length using Yule's K Characteristic, Simpson's D, Honoré's R (hapax legomena scaling), Sichel's S (dislegomena ratio), Brunét's W, and Moving-Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR).

methods.name: Mosteller & Wallace Function-Word Discriminant Analysis
methods.formula_summary: Log-odds / Bayesian & Linear Discriminant weighting on topic-independent marker words ('upon', 'whilst', 'enough', etc.)
methods.description: Landmark statistical study resolving the 12 disputed Federalist Papers by modeling rates of non-contextual function words (prepositions, conjunctions, adverbs) whose usage is invariant to political topic.

methods.name: Kilgarriff's Chi-Squared (χ²) Distance
methods.formula_summary: chi^2(A, B) = sum_{w in MFW} (O_{w,A} - E_{w,A})^2 / E_{w,A} + (O_{w,B} - E_{w,B})^2 / E_{w,B}
methods.description: Measures corpus similarity and authorship by computing the Pearson chi-squared statistic over raw token counts of the top-N most frequent words between a candidate author's subcorpus and an unknown text.

methods.name: Burrows's Classic Delta (Manhattan Z-Score Distance)
methods.description: The foundational modern stylometric metric: standardizes relative frequencies of the M Most Frequent Words (MFWs) into corpus z-scores so all features have equal variance, then computes mean absolute (L1 / Manhattan) distance.

methods.name: Argamon's Quadratic Delta (Euclidean Z-Score Distance)
methods.description: Probabilistic derivation of Burrows's Delta under Gaussian independence assumptions, replacing the L1 norm on z-scores with the L2 (Euclidean) distance.

methods.name: Cosine Delta (Würzburg Delta)
methods.authors: Peter W. H. Smith & W. Aldridge (2011); Stefan Evert, Thomas Proisl, Fotis Jannidis et al. (2017)
methods.description: Normalizes z-score vectors to the unit hypersphere before computing angular (cosine) distance. Demonstrated by Evert et al. (2017) to outperform classic Burrows's Delta across languages, text lengths, and large MFW sizes.

methods.name: Eder's Delta (Rank-Weighted Manhattan Z-Score Distance)
methods.authors: Maciej Eder, Jan Rybicki & Mike Kestemont
methods.description: Weights each feature in the MFW list by its inverse frequency rank so that higher-frequency grammatical words exert stronger influence than lower-ranked words.

methods.name: Character N-Gram Profile Attribution (CNG)
methods.authors: Vlado Kešelj et al. (2003); Efstathios Stamatatos (2009)
methods.formula_summary: Cosine / Delta distance over top-K character 3-grams and 4-grams
methods.description: Captures sub-word prefixes, suffixes, inflectional morphemes, word boundaries, and punctuation-whitespace habits without requiring language-specific lemmatizers.

methods.name: Syntactic Complexity, Sentence Rhythm & Punctuation Fingerprinting
methods.authors: E. Stamatatos et al. (2000); H. Baayen et al. (1996)
methods.formula_summary: Sentence length distribution moments + punctuation rates per 1,000 tokens (; : , — ? ! ( )) + readability indices
methods.description: Measures clause hierarchy and authorial cadence via sentence-length distributions, semicolon/colon/dash habits, and readability complexity metrics.

methods.name: Koppel & Winter's General Imposters (GI) Authorship Verification
methods.authors: Moshe Koppel & Yaron Winter (2014); Mike Kestemont et al. (2016)
methods.formula_summary: S(X, C) = (1/K) * sum_{k=1}^K I[ min_{c in C} d_{F_k}(X, c) < min_{imp in I_k} d_{F_k}(X, imp) ]
methods.description: Gold-standard open-set authorship verification algorithm: across K Monte Carlo iterations, randomly samples 50% of features and a subset of distractor ('imposter') documents, measuring the proportion of iterations where the disputed text is closer to the candidate author than to all sampled imposters.

methods.name: Multivariate & Supervised Machine Learning Attribution (SVM, Logistic Regression, PCA, Ward Clustering)
methods.authors: J. F. Burrows (1987 PCA); G. Fung (2003 SVM); E. Stamatatos (2009)
methods.formula_summary: Linear SVM / L2 Logistic Regression / PCA + Ward Hierarchical Clustering on composite stylometric feature matrices
methods.description: Combines function-word frequencies, lexical diversity, sentence rhythm, punctuation density, and character n-grams into calibrated supervised classifiers and unsupervised PCA/dendrogram projections.

external_software.name: stylo (R Package)
external_software.authors_or_org: Computational Stylistics Group (Maciej Eder, Jan Rybicki, Mike Kestemont)
external_software.key_capabilities: De facto standard in Digital Humanities for Delta (Burrows, Cosine, Eder), PCA, Bootstrap Consensus Trees, Rolling Stylometry, and General Imposters (`imposters()`).

external_software.name: faststylometry
external_software.key_capabilities: Burrows's Delta implementation with logistic-calibrated probability estimation for same-author vs. different-author pairs.

external_software.name: StyloMetrix
external_software.key_capabilities: Interpretable grammatical, syntactic, and lexical feature vectors built on spaCy.

external_software.name: pystyl
external_software.key_capabilities: Python stylometry preprocessing, MFW vectorization, distance matrices, and clustering.

external_software.name: Programming Historian Stylometry Suite
external_software.key_capabilities: Canonical Python implementations of Mendenhall's Characteristic Curves, Kilgarriff's Chi-Squared, and Burrows's Delta on The Federalist Papers.

external_software.name: PAN Clef Shared Tasks on Digital Text Forensics and Stylometry
external_software.key_capabilities: Annual benchmark datasets and evaluation harnesses for authorship attribution, authorship verification, style change detection, and AI text detection.

benchmark_corpora.name: The Federalist Papers (1787–1788)
benchmark_corpora.historical_problem: 85 essays published under the shared pseudonym 'Publius'. 51 undisputed by Hamilton, 14 undisputed by Madison, 5 by Jay (#2-5, #64), 3 joint (#18-20), and 12 famous disputed essays (#49-58, #62-63) claimed by both Hamilton and Madison.

benchmark_corpora.name: 19th-Century Classic Literature Benchmark Corpus
benchmark_corpora.historical_problem: Multi-author literary attribution across 15 full novels (~1.9M words), including cross-genre test cases such as attributing Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's science-fiction adventure 'The Lost World' against H. G. Wells's science-fiction romances and distinguishing Victorian contemporaries.

upon_vs_on.note: Hamilton uses 'upon' ~3.2 per 1,000 words vs. Madison's ~0.16 per 1,000 words.

while_vs_whilst.note: Hamilton almost exclusively uses 'while'; Madison almost exclusively uses 'whilst'.

enough.note: Hamilton uses 'enough' regularly; Madison virtually never uses it in the Federalist.

consequently.note: Madison uses 'consequently' at a much higher rate than Hamilton.
